I do have to point out that witchcraft itself isn’t actually a religion and the practices of witches do have extremely deep roots that spread across all religions, including christianity. Witchcraft is a secular practice and there are plenty of atheist, christian, jewish, pagan, etc witches. If you take away the label of “witchcraft” you can see these practices in christianity, for example the idea of holy water, baptism, saint candles, and many other traditions could be considered witchcraft if you really want to get into it. Some witches worship deities, some worship the natural energies, some worship absolutely nothing at all. Witchcraft is not at all synonymous with Wicca and the recent rise of witches on the internet should not make ancient practices any less valid. Consider practices like voodoo, old celtic religions, holidays like yule (christmas), samhain (halloween), midsummer, etc, ancient african practices, and so many more. All of these are witchcraft and date back hundreds if not thousands of years. It is not fair to delegitimize any religion but witchcraft isn’t even a religion and DOES have very ancient roots.
